summary: The Steiner tree routing strategy was confirmed to outperform the per-destination Dijkstra shortest-path baseline, achieving a score of 0.1341 vs 0.0955 (40.4% improvement). The core mechanism — sharing relay paths across destinations to reduce total unique edge cost — is validated, though the absolute score remains low (0.13 out of 100), indicating substantial room for further optimization.
key_points: CONFIRMED: Steiner tree routing (score 0.1341) beats Dijkstra baseline (score 0.0955) by 40.4%, validating that shared relay paths reduce broadcast cost.
Observed treatment score (0.1341) was slightly below the designer's probe estimate (0.154), likely due to differences between probe and full 5-scenario evaluator — directional effect holds strongly.

Scores remain very low (~0.13/100), meaning total cost is still ~$645. Major cost drivers (egress cost, instance cost from transfer time) are not yet aggressively optimized — partition-level load balancing, multi-path splitting, and bandwidth-aware routing are untested strategies that could yield large further gains.

Next iterations should explore: (1) splitting partitions across diverse paths to reduce bandwidth bottlenecks and transfer time, (2) bandwidth-aware edge weighting to minimize the instance cost component, and (3) hybrid cost+time optimization rather than pure cost minimization.
